title: Common pointed refinement of residual SNC charts
statement: Let p be a positive prime and k a field of characteristic p. Let Y be a regular separated finite-type k-scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme] and D a strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], with finitely many distinct integral regular labelled components C_i whose intersections are regular of the expected codimension. Fix a set I of component labels. In the open Y_I obtained by deleting components outside I, let S be the reduced intersection of the components in I. Use the residual-chart and parameter-tower data of [def-sfb-snc-residual-chart-data]. Then every finite family of residual charts with prescribed geometric residual points above one geometric stratum point admits one common residual chart, etale base maps, compatible henselization and universal-cover maps, compatible unit changes of all parameter-root towers, and lifted points satisfying the displayed base and point squares. No covering-family assertion is made; the family may have zero members.

Agent assembly with Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 7.4.3 and the pointed finite-etale cover system; SNC parameter geometry: ILO VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), IX Proposition 2.1, pp.133–134. Combined residual-neighborhood statement, not a verbatim single-tag theorem.

proof.text: Take the finite pointed fibre product of the affine etale base charts and a reference stratum chart through the given point. Choose an affine neighbourhood of the induced point and shrink its residual scheme to the connected regular component through that point. This works for an empty input family by retaining the reference chart.

proof.text: Use the common pointed affine refinement theorem and the canonical maps of pair henselizations. Pointed finite-etale functoriality gives maps of the affine universal covers and their residual quotients. If the input charts have different marked points, a path between their fibre functors identifies their universal covers and supplies the lifts of the prescribed common point.

proof.text: Corresponding labelled Cartier equations differ by units. Choose compatible fibre roots of these units and lift them to the common universal cover by normalized splitting. The unit-coordinate comparison theorem gives maps of finite, full, reduced and punctured parameter-root algebras.

proof.text: Check each displayed coefficient and generator formula, the transition and inclusion squares and the quotient-descent squares. Define the input lifted points by composition from the common lift; their base equations follow from the coefficient squares. For zero labels all root-coordinate requirements are vacuous and the maps are the coefficient maps.

theorem exists_sncResidualChart_common_refinement
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p]
    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (y : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType y] [QuasiCompact y] [IsSeparated y]
    (hY : IsRegularScheme Y) (D : Y.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : IsStrictNormalCrossingsBoundary D)
    (a : ℕ) (C : Fin a → Y.IdealSheafData)
    (hC : Function.Injective (fun i ↦ (C i).support) ∧
      (∀ i, IsIntegral (C i).subscheme ∧ IsRegularScheme (C i).subscheme) ∧
      D.support = ⨆ i, (C i).support ∧
      ∀ s : Finset (Fin a), ∀ z : (⨆ i ∈ s, C i).subscheme,
        IsRegularScheme (⨆ i ∈ s, C i).subscheme ∧
        ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk ((⨆ i ∈ s, C i).subschemeι z)) =
          ringKrullDim ((⨆ i ∈ s, C i).subscheme.presheaf.stalk z) + (s.card : ℕ))
    (I : Finset (Fin a))
    (q : ℕ) (Q : Fin q → SNCResidualChart p C I)
      (Ω' : Type u) [Field Ω'] [IsAlgClosed Ω']
      (s : Spec (.of Ω') ⟶ (sncStratumIdeal C I).subscheme)
      (sv : ∀ d : Fin q,
        Spec (.of Ω') ⟶ Spec (.of ((Q d).B ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (Q d).t))))
    (hsv : ∀ d, sv d ≫ (Q d).residualIso.hom ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = s) :
    ∃ (R : SNCResidualChart p C I)
      (sr : Spec (.of Ω') ⟶ Spec (.of (R.B ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range R.t))))
      (f : ∀ d : Fin q, SNCResidualRefinement (Q d) R)
      (ur : Spec (.of Ω') ⟶ Spec R.H)
      (uv : ∀ d : Fin q, Spec (.of Ω') ⟶ Spec (Q d).H),
      sr ≫ R.residualIso.hom ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = s ∧
      ur ≫ Spec.map R.b = sr ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range R.t)))) ∧
      (∀ d, ur ≫ Spec.map (f d).lift = uv d) ∧
      (∀ d, uv d ≫ Spec.map (Q d).b =
        sv d ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range (Q d).t))))) ∧
      ∀ d, sr ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range R.t)))) ≫ Spec.map (f d).base =
        sv d ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range (Q d).t))))
